newsitem.title: UK: British ex-minister to criticise colleague - report.
newsitem.headline: British ex-minister to criticise colleague - report.

text.p: Former British prisons minister Ann Widdecombe will ask this week to make a statement in parliament about the conduct of Michael Howard, her former boss at the Home Office, the Financial Times reported on Tuesday.

In a move that may cast a shadow over Howard's bid for the leadership of the opposition Conservative Party, Widdecombe was due to meet the speaker of the House of Commons on Thursday, the newspaper said.
She will ask permission to make a statement on Howard's handling of a crisis in the Prison Service which led to the dismissal by Howard of the organisation's director, Derek Lewis, in 1995.
Widdecombe has publicly accused Howard of misleading parliament over the affair.
Howard, one of six men competing to succeed John Major as leader of the Conservative Party following its heavy election defeat by Labour on May 1, has strenuously denied the allegations.
The Financial Times quoted an aide to Howard as saying the allegations were "completely untrue".
Widdecombe has not divulged the precise details of her complaint about Howard.
